text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says the person who attacked him in Hungary might have been a foreigner as he did not speak Turkish.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller defends organised crime boss Abdullah Catli by saying those who kill for the state are honourable people.
- MPs show their distate for goverment draft law to restrict the press by not attending parliamentary debate on the issue.
- Kiwi fruit orchards are replacing tea planting lands in the Black Sea region.
- Tight security measures taken for the 18th anniversary on Wednesday of the foundation of the Kurdistan Workers Party rebel group.
- Three of the 124 Islamist arsonists charged with killing 37 people in 1993 flee Turkey.
- The Turkish lira weakened to 101,000 against the U.S. currency.
- Ninety thousand people applied for the 2,500 vacancies in Social Insurance Institution.
- Civil servants protest at pay rise for the first half of 1997.
